title: Prepare Markup for open sourcing
description: Harry wants to open source Markup: MIT licence, demo video, marketing hook in README, and a message to share with friends. Also audit the repo for anything that should not be public.
close_reason: Licence, demo video, README and launch copy prepared; publication steps left for Harry

title: Robust feedback export: no phantom pins, checklist, per-point report, grouping, screenshot dedupe, export warning
description: A real site review exported 23 marks of which 12 were empty accidental pins, split thoughts across pins, 32 mostly duplicate screenshots and a prompt that never asked the agent to account for each point; an agent missed a point. Fix: (1) click with editor open only closes it, empty new comment pins discarded; (2) checklist at top of feedback.md counting marks with notes, note-less marks secondary; (3) prompt and --wait output state the count and ask for a per-point report; (4) group marks on the same element; (5) dedupe overviews and identical close-ups; (6) warn about note-less marks before export.
close_reason: All six changes implemented with smoke tests; npm test passes. Uncommitted pending Harry's review.

title: Review pages served by a dev server (open a URL, not just a file)
description:
Markup opens files only. Apps that exist only behind a dev server (for example localhost:5173) cannot be reviewed live; today the workaround is a built HTML file or a screenshot.

Idea: proxy every non-/__markup__/ path to the target server so the page stays same-origin with the app (needed for element anchoring and selectors). Needs websocket pass-through for hot reload, and no data-mk-line tagging (source lines mean nothing for transformed output). Keep the rule that nothing reachable from a web page accepts a path or URL: the target comes from the command line or a field in the app's own UI.

title: Open a file by dropping it on the Dock icon or with Open With
description: Dropping an HTML/PDF/image on Markup.app in the Dock, or Finder's Open With, should open it in Markup. macOS delivers these as Apple Events, which the current shell-script launcher cannot receive. Needs a small native launcher (swiftc is available on Harry's Mac) that declares CFBundleDocumentTypes and forwards the paths to 'server.js <file>'.

title: Running window shows under a Chrome icon, not the Markup icon
description:
Markup.app (scripts/build-app.sh) is a launcher: it starts server.js and exits. The window is a second Chrome instance, so while Markup is open the Dock shows a Chrome icon for it and the Markup icon has no running dot.

A native wrapper (small Swift app that stays running, owns the node child and handles reopen) would give a running dot and a single place to quit, but the window would still belong to Chrome. A true single Dock identity needs Chrome running from inside the bundle or a Chrome app shim; both are fragile across Chrome updates. Decide whether it is worth it.

title: Note labels overlap each other and cover nearby content
description: When marks sit close together their note labels stack on top of one another, and a label tab above a box covers whatever is directly above it (visible in the exported close-ups). The 'Notes on page' toggle is the current escape hatch. Options: nudge labels apart, shorten them when crowded, or draw a leader line to a label placed in free space.
